items.readable_text:
Content:
We can use the standard algorithm for division to divide three-digit-numbers by two-digit numbers.

Content:
For example, what is the value of [MATH: 528 \div 24?]

Content:
We start by writing down the question using long division notation:

Content:
| | [MATH: 24] | [MATH: \!\!\require{enclose}\enclose{longdiv}{5 {\:\phantom{|}} 2 {\:\phantom{|}} 8}] | | | | |

Content:
First, we would consider the hundreds, but [MATH: 24] doesn't go into [MATH: \color{red}5.] So instead, we consider the hundreds and tens.
Notice that [MATH: 24] goes [MATH: {\color{blue}2}] times into [MATH: {\color{red}52}.] So, we get:

Content:
| | | | [MATH: \color{blue}2] | | / | [MATH: 24] | [MATH: \!\!\require{enclose}\enclose{longdiv}{{\color{red}5} {\:\phantom{|}} {\color{red}2} {\:\phantom{|}} 8}] | / | [MATH: -\!\!\!\!] | [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 8] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}\,\downarrow] | / | | | [MATH: 4] | [MATH: \color{lightgray}8] | | | Write over tens: [MATH: \color{blue}2] | / | Multiply: [MATH: 24 \times {\color{blue}2} = 48] | / | Subtract: [MATH: {\color{red}52} - 48 = 4] | / | Bring down: [MATH: 8] | |

Content:
Finally, notice that [MATH: 24] goes [MATH: {\color{blue}2}] times into [MATH: {\color{red}48}.] So, we get:

Content:
| | | | [MATH: 2] | [MATH: \color{blue}2] | / | [MATH: 24] | [MATH: \!\!\require{enclose}\enclose{longdiv}{5 {\:\phantom{|}} 2 {\:\phantom{|}} 8}] | / | [MATH: -\!\!\!\!] | [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 8] | | / | | | [MATH: \color{red}4] | [MATH: \color{red}8] | / | | [MATH: -\!\!\!\!] | [MATH: 4] | [MATH: 8] | / | | | [MATH: \phantom{0}] | [MATH: 0] | | | Write over ones: [MATH: \color{blue}2] | / | Multiply: [MATH: 24 \times {\color{blue}2} = 48] | / | Subtract: [MATH: {\color{red}48} - 48 = 0] | |

Content:
We've gone through all the digits, so the division is done.

Content:
Therefore,
[MATH: 528 \div 24 = 22 \, .]
